asr.full_text: Hi everyone, James Z here. Have anyone of you tried crypto staking which usually gives more than 60% APY returns for storing your cryptocurrencies on their platform? Today we look at Singapore registered CakeDefi which gives about 70% APY net return on your investments. Meaning your $1,000 can potentially become one thousand seven hundred dollars in one year. Does it sound too good to be true, or is it potentially a rug pull where you can lose all your coins? There are so many ways your investments may turn out, let's find out. CakeDeFi was founded by Dr Julian Hobbs and Eugene Chua, which they aim to solve major financial pain points in people's life. they claim to provide DeFi services such as liquidity mining, staking, lending, freezer to generate constant cash flow for yourself. Basically it's different channels where you can use your crypto to earn passive income. The following points I'll be touching on applies to all DeFi services, not just CAKE DeFi, as they all function similarly and faces the same risk. We'll look at liquidity mining first. You can see the APR for mining ranges from 50 to 65% depending on the coin. For mining to operate they need a liquidity pull with that comprise of 2 different coins, as you can see, they offer BTC, LTC, USDC and a few more coins, including dogecoin, and they are all paired up with the main currency or the main coin, which is the DeFi coin Your deposited funds will be part of this pool where CakeDeFi would give you rewards every 24 hours, but do note, they will take a 15% cut of the total rewards. However, liquidity mining risk impermanent loss. It is when the price of assets locked up in a liquidity pool changes after being deposited and creates an unrealised loss as compared to holding a cryptocurrencies wallet. These changes occur for two main reasons and has to do with Automated Market Makers System. 1. Defined pools always maintain an equal ratio of assets in the pool. For example, an USDT and DFI pool will have a fixed ratio of 1 is to 2, respectively. It means, every $1 of USDT in the pool, there MUST be $2's worth of DeFi coin. If you intend to deposit $100 dollars into USDT, you HAVE to deposit $200 dollars into DeFi. 200 dollars into DFI. next any crypto movement will create an imbalance in the pool such as redrawing 10 USDT and zero DFI so for cake defy to maintain the one is the two ratio they rely on arbitrage traders to align pool asset prices with the current market value. For example, if the market price of DFI Coin is $2 but the value of the DFI coin in this pool is only $1.5, RBA will spot the discrepancies and will be financially incentivized to add DFI Coin tokens to bump the price back up to 2 dollars. If arbitrage traders added DFI to take out USDT, the ratio of coins changes. In order to regain balance, the liquidity pool automatically increases the price of in higher supply and reduce price of token in lower supply which is DFI is to encourage arbitrage traders to rebalance the pool. Once the pool rebalance, the rise in the value of liquidity pool is often less than the value of the assets if held by the lending protocol, so that is called the impermanent loss. The unrealised loss is only permanent if you decide to redraw your funds. Personally, I've not tried this because staking is a better choice. If you are interested in liquidity mining, the best way to mitigate impermanent losses is to provide liquidity to a pool containing less volatile assets such as stablecoins that I just mentioned USDT USDC because only one side of the scale is fluctuating. Next, we are going to look at Staking. Currently, DFICoin gives about 70% APY, which is higher than liquidity mining. But before you jump onto the wagon, what is staking? Staking serves a similar function to mining. Staking pool is like an interest saving account, your DeFi coin will put to work on the blockchain. Cryptocurrencies that allow staking uses a consensus mechanism called proof of stake which is a way to ensure that all transactions are verified and secured without a bank to process in the middle, your stake assets become part of that process. The exact implementations vary from project to project, but technically your token queues up for the chance to add a new block onto the blockchain in exchange for reward. CakeDeFi rewards you every 12 hours for staking, the displayed APY is net of fees, so that is the ROI you are looking at. You can choose to withdraw anytime. Here is the table which I compiled to show you some insights. You can also find the real-time updates of my Cape Defined portfolio using the google link in my description box below. The next option is lending. Each lending period lasts for four weeks you should a sex will be locked the base guaranteed return api will be shown and if the coin prices hit a certain target at a point of maturity you receive additional bonuses okay example assuming Bitcoin price is a ten thousand when you enter the contract the guaranteed return is 5% per annum and a bonus of 2.5%, if Bitcoin prices reaches $12,500 at the point when contract expires. You will then be entitled to the bonus giving you a total of 7.5% per annum. The perk is – there isn't any fees involved! Freezers The last is freezers, where you lock your funds up and earn higher returns. You can choose which coin and how long you want to keep them frozen, ranging from 1 month to 10 years. They followed robot advisors style, where you'll be given a projected figure after years of investements. But guys! This is cryptos, it may be worth 0 dollars in the future, so please don't use that graph as a benchmark. Now we have to be ready for this risk should you try Kade Define or any other DeFi services. I'm hoping this will not happen but there are platforms out there that dea a rug pull. If you are wondering what rug pull is, it is a new type of EXICSCAM where the 5 of developers create a new token, peddle it up to a leading cryptocurrencies such as tether or ether and setup a liquidity pool. They then market the newly created tokens and encourage people to deposit money into the pool, often promising extremely high use. A good example is billion dollar rugby pool came in 2020 when Sushiswap developer Chef Nomi unexpectedly liquidated his sushi tokens after raising over a billion dollars in collateral. The price of the token fell to zero in what is remembered as one of the most dramatic moments in DeFi Unless your DeFi is run by a government agency This risk applies to all platforms The y-only plays $500 and nothing more The 2nd risk is the pricing of the coin will leave you with unrealized loss Even if you are earning 70% APY Even though you are earning interest% APY. Even though they are earning interest, they are paid in coins so the price of the coins is dependent on the marketplace. Unless the PR is in stablecoins, value of the investments will fluctuate. there are so many more risks such as flange loan attack, theft and Failure which I'll leave into another video. My experience with Caked EFI has been okay thus far and I'm only going to stake $500, I won't be trying the other 3 There are some things that I can't judge but you may want to Google more into the founders before you decide to invest. I hope my insights provide you with more information on CAKEFY. I'm also exploring another similar platform called Coachcoin, which gives you 700% plus APY. Waterhedge, right? It's definitely a Ponzi scheme alert but I still decided to play around with it. Let's see how QRCity kills JimZee! Subscribe and like this video if you want to learn more about my plights first hand. I won't be sharing any referral links because I'm still quite sceptical about CAKETDIFY. Hit me up in the comments below if you have any questions. I'll put up an excel link where you can track my CAKETDIFY ROI. Sharing is caring. Always be careful when it comes to crypto! Share this video with your friends if they're interested in this platform. Stay tuned and stay safe. Jimzi, signing off!
